JUDGMENT Wife , child and parents of deceased Santhosh filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.10,00,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 alleging that on 30.06.2018 at 11.30 p.m. , when Santhosh was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JU-2853 on Bengaluru- Magadi road in front of R.V.L. Kalyana Mantapa, Honnaganahatti village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru driver of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 drove the same negligently from opposite direction, overtook another tipper lorry , drove the lorry to the wrong part of the road , dashed the same to the motorcycle , made Santhosh to fell on the road, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Santhosh .
2. As on the date of accident deceased Santhosh being aged 34 years , used to earn Rs.2,50,205/p.m.
by working as Engineer at Flex Flextronics Manufacturing (Singapore) , Pvt. Ltd., Singapore , used to contribute the entire income to the family.
3. Regarding accident Tavarekere police registered a case in crime No.201/2018 against the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 .

2 4.
In response to the notice, respondent No.1 owner of the tipper lorry appeared through his Advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

5. In response to the notice respondent No.2, insurance company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident , age,
occupation and income of the deceased.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 09.03.2022, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-41-B-9966 by its driver dashed to the deceased Sri Santhosh who was riding Yamaha Fafkino Scooter bearing reg. No.KA-05- JU-2853 and he succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 30.06.2018?
2.
Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of deceased himself?

3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
4.
What order?

7. On 04.06.2022, 18.06.2022, 26.09.2022 petitioner No.1 Sindhu H.A., W/o. Santhosh deposed as PW1 and produced 16 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... In the Negative, Issue No.3 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.28,90,096/- with current and future interest at 6%p..a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.4 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issues No.1 and 2 :- In the evidence PW1 stated that on 30.06.2018 at 11.30 p.m. , when Santhosh was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JU-2853 on Bengaluru- Magadi road, in front of R.V.L. Kalyana Mantapa, Honnaganahatti village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru driver of a Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B- 9966 drove the same negligently from opposite direction, on the wrong part of the road, dashed the same to the motorcycle, made Santhosh to fell on the road, thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Santhosh .

3 11.
In the written statement respondent No. 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident .
12. In the cross-examination, PW1 admitted that she never witnessed the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.201/2018 registered by Tavarekere police on 01.07.2018 at 00.30 hours against the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC regarding accidental death of Santhosh in view of dashing of the lorry on the basis of the complaint filed by petitioner No.4 Siddalingaswamy, S/o. P.S.Siddaiah, father of deceased Santhosh.
14. Ex
. P.2 is the copy of the complaint filed by Siddalingaswamy.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar dated 01.07.2018.

Ex.P.4 is the copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report dated 04.07.2018 in which damage noticed by the Motor Vehicle Inspector in the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA- 41-B-9966 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JU-2853 are mentioned.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of the inquest mahazar .

Ex.P.7 is the copy of the P.M.Report.
15.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of chargesheet filed by Tavarekere police in crime No.201/2018 against Mallikarjun, S/o. Gaddeppa, driver of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,304(A) of IPC .
In the police records name of deceased Santhosh is noted as rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JU-2853 and victim of the accident.

16. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of police records regarding reason,
mode and consequence of the accident.

17. Hence, I have concluded that on 30.06.2018 at 11.30 p.m. , when Santhosh was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JU-2853 on Bengaluru- Magadi road in front of R.V.L. Kalyana Mantapa, Honnaganahatti village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru, Mallikarjun, S/o. Gaddeppa,
negligently drove lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 from opposite direction, dashed the same to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JU-2853 , thereby caused the accident, caused instantaneous death of Santhosh .
Hence, I answer issue No. 1 in the Affirmative and issue No,2 in the Negative.
18. Issue No.3:

In the evidence PW1/Sindhu , W/o. Santhosh stated that as on the date of accident her husband deceased Santhosh being aged 34 years, used to earn $3,689.75 per month (Indian currency Rs.2,50,205/p.m.) by working as Engineer at Flex Flextronics Manufacturing, Singapore ,
Pvt. Ltd., Singapore) and used to contribute entire income to the family and her husband deceased Santhosh having good prospects in future job.
19. In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of the deceased.
20. In the cross-examination, PW1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident deceased Santhosh was aged about 36 years.
PW1 stated that deceased Santhosh was working as Testing Engineer at Flex Flextronics Manufacturing (Singapore) , Pvt. Ltd., Company Singapore .

PW1 Sindhu H.A vs Ramesh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104914643/
4 admitted that since last two years as on the date of accident her husband has been residing in Bengaluru and since last 2 years her husband did not engage in any work.
PW1 stated about production of documents regarding earning of Rs.2,50,205/p.m. by her husband.
PW1 denied the suggestion that documents produced at Ex.P.13 to P.15 are not pertaining to deceased Santhosh.
PW1 admitted that documents marked at Ex.P.16 does not bear seal and signature of the company.
PW1 admitted that documents marked at Ex.P.11 is not concerned with the treatment of her husband.
21. In the police records age of the deceased is noted as 34 years.
In the copy of the aadhar card and driving licence date of birth of the deceased Santhosh is noted as 30.04.1984.
The documents marked at Ex.P.9, 10, 12, 16 regarding occupation and income of deceased Santhosh are of the year 2016.
22. In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of deceased Santhosh for the year 2018, the year of accident.

There is no dispute that the present petitioners are the wife,
child and parents of deceased Santhosh.

23. Hence, I have calculated compensation under the head of loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Santhosh as on the 34 years date of accident - Monthly notional income of deceased - Rs.12,500/- Santhosh as on the date of a c c i d e n t A d d : 5 0 % f u t u r e p r o s p e c t s R s . 1 8 , 7 5 0 / -
12,500x50/100=6,250+12,500=18,750 Less : 1/ 4th towards personal expenses of Rs.14,063/- the deceased Santhosh (18,750 - 4,687/- = 14,063) Annual income of the deceased 14,063x12 Rs.1,68,756/- Loss of dependency 1,68,756x16 Rs.27,00,096/-
24.
Hence, I award Rs.27,00,096/- towards loss of dependency.

Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses , Rs.40,000/- towards spousal consortium to petitioner No.1,
Rs.40,000/- towards parental consortium to petitioner No.2, Rs.80,000/- towards filial consortium to petitioners No.3 and 4, parents of deceased Santhosh at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each 25.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being wife , child and parents of deceased Santhosh are entitle to receive Rs.28,90,096/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
as compensation from the respondents.

. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1.
Loss of dependency 27,00,096-00 2. Loss of estate 15,000-00
3. Funeral expenses 15,000-00 Sindhu H.A vs Ramesh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104914643/
5 4. Loss of Consortium to 1,60,000-00 petitioners No.1to 4 at Rs.40,000/each
Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly.
26. Issue No.4:

In the written statement , respondent No.2, insurance company admitted the subsistence of policy with respect to Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 as on the date of accident and sought permission to defend the case under Section 170 of IMV Act.
Xerox copy of DL No.KA3620120012639 shows that as on the date of accident Mallikarjun , S/o. Gaddeppa had licence to drive Transport vehicle.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents No.1 and 2 to pay compensation to the petitioners,
Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.28,90,096/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-41-B-9966 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally .

After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners No.1,3 and 4 may be released by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.

Entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioner No.2 (minor) shall be deposited in any bank in the name of petitioner No.2 till she attain the age of 19 years without permitting to create any encumbrances and reserving liberty to her mother petitioner No.1/guardian to withdraw periodical interest once in 3 months in accordance with law.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
